what_its_for: Minocycline is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as acne, urinary tract infections, respiratory infections, skin infections, and certain sexually transmitted infections. It works by stopping the growth of bacteria in your body.
how_to_take: Take minocycline exactly as your doctor prescribed. You may take it with or without food, but taking it with food or a full glass of water (8 ounces) can help prevent stomach upset and irritation of your esophagus (swallowing tube). Do NOT lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking your dose. Swallow capsules or tablets whole — do not crush, break, or chew them. If you are using the topical (skin) form, apply a thin layer to the affected area only and do not get it in your eyes, mouth, or nose.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 50 to 100 mg taken twice daily, or as directed by your doctor. Extended-release tablets (Solodyn) are typically taken once daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose depends on the condition being treated and your weight. Complete the full course of antibiotics even if you start feeling better early — stopping too soon can allow the infection to return.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store minocycline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not use minocycline past its expiration date — expired tetracycline-type antibiotics like minocycline can be harmful.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking minocycline with antacids, calcium supplements, iron supplements, or dairy products (like milk or yogurt) within 2 hours of your dose, as these can reduce how well the medication works. Avoid prolonged sun exposure and tanning beds, as minocycline makes your skin much more sensitive to sunburn — wear sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Do not take minocycline during pregnancy or while breastfeeding without talking to your doctor first. Avoid giving this medication to children under 8 years old unless specifically directed by a doctor, as it can permanently stain developing teeth. Limit alcohol use during treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away or seek emergency care if you experience: severe headache, blurred or double vision, or vision changes (could be a sign of increased pressure in the brain); yellowing of your skin or eyes; dark urine or pale stools; severe skin rash, blistering, or peeling; difficulty swallowing or severe heartburn (esophagus irritation); signs of a severe allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; joint pain or swelling; unusual bruising or bleeding; or severe diarrhea or stomach cramping that does not go away (could be a sign of a serious gut infection called C. diff).
when_it_works: For bacterial infections, you may start to feel better within a few days, but it is important to finish the full course of treatment. For acne, improvement is usually gradual — many people notice less redness and fewer breakouts after 4 to 6 weeks of use, with the best results often seen after 3 months of consistent treatment.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Minocycline should NOT be used during pregnancy as it can harm the developing baby, particularly affecting bone growth and causing permanent tooth discoloration. Talk to your doctor immediately if you become pregnant while taking this medication. Children under 8 years old: Generally should NOT be used in young children because it can cause permanent gray, yellow, or brown staining of teeth and affect bone development. Older adults: Use with caution; kidney function should be monitored. Patients with kidney or liver disease: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose or monitor you more closely. Always inform your doctor about all medical conditions and medications you are taking, including vitamins and herbal supplements.
